newsitem.title: USA: A new cost-cutting kid arrives in tungsten town.
newsitem.headline: A new cost-cutting kid arrives in tungsten town.

text.p: North American Tungsten aims to be the new low-cost kid on the tungsten block following its takeover of assets formerly held by Canada Tungsten Inc.
Armed with cost-cutting technology, North American Tungsten's goal is to restart mining, a company official said.

Earlier Thursday North American Tungsten said it had inked a deal with Aur Resources - which had merged with Canada Tungsten - to buy the CanTung mine in Northwest Territories, the MacTung property near CanTung, and the Hemerdon property in England.
The company will also take a half share in the Californian 30,000 metric tonne units (MTU) per year ammonium meta-tungstate plant, the balance held by Aur.
Tungsten is a strategic metal used to make cutting equipment, light bulb filaments, heavy metal components, catalysts and tool steels.
China is the world's dominant supplier of tungsten.
The C$5 million deal, subject to due diligence by North American Tungsten and approval by the Vancouver Stock Exchange, is set for completion within 60 days.

North American Tungsten spokesman Ron Shenton said the company will use technology bought from the U.S. Department of Mines to process tungsten concentrates more cheaply than conventional technology can.
"We have been tweaking it and playing with it," Shenton said, referring to the gas barging technology. "It reduces production costs of tungsten by up to 50 percent."
"We are confident it's (the technology) proven for tungsten," Shenton said.
No full scale commercial unit has been set up using the technology, but small amounts of saleable concentrates have been produced.
The tungsten mines and properties, coupled with the production technology, will make North American Tungsten an integrated producer, Shenton said.

The CanTung mine has over three years of proven reserves based on a mineable rate of 1,100 tonnes per day of ore. In addition to all the serviced mill facilities, a full townsite exists for production employess, North American Tungsten said in a statement.

At current tungsten market prices, "CanTung is pretty close to breakeven right now," Shenton said."One of the main goals is to vertically integrate our technology into that, and then it becomes profitable."
Providing we close within 60 days, it would be another four to five months after that before we would be looking at ramping up (CanTung)," Shenton said.
"The processing facility is already receiving ore from various places and processing it, so we would go into cash flow immediately," he added.
North American Tungsten expected metal prices to continue rising.

"We see a supply and demand problem going on out there. We see consumption continuing up, and most of the world's mines cannot come back up," Shenton said. "When the Chinese flooded the market 10 to 15 years ago, it put a lot of them (Western mines) under, and we don't anticipate most of them coming back on."
Avocet Mining , the Western world's biggest producer of the hard metal, late last year said stockpiles may not be able to plug what it sees as a supply shortfall for much longer.
Avocet forecast a supply gap of 14,000 tonnes of primary tungsten metal this year, consumption pegged at 38,800 tonnes in 1996.
((Huw Jones, New York Commodities 212-849-1646))
